text:
Marathon Petroleum rose modestly today, continuing a strong rebound from a week-long dip that saw the stock fall 6.76% through November 6th. The climb reflects tightness in refined products: heating oil prices have spiked 59% from last winter, and diesel and heating oil inventories remain lean at 103.33 million barrels. Refineries are humming at 95.2% utilization, positioning refiners to profit from the gap between crude costs (holding steady around $90 per barrel) and the premium prices for finished fuels heading into winter.

The broader backdrop is shifting toward refiner advantage. Russian crude production has recovered after geopolitical turbulence, pushing global oil into oversupply—which typically means cheaper feedstock for refiners. At the same time, heating season demand is real and pressing: consumers are scrambling to cover oil bills as prices have more than doubled year-over-year. This seasonal squeeze on refined products, combined with elevated utilization rates and moderate crude prices, supports margins for companies like Marathon that turn oil into diesel and heating oil.
